title: At the Doctor's Office
description: Learn to describe symptoms and understand doctor instructions
objectives: Describe how you feel (I have a headache / My stomach hurts)
Answer the doctor's questions about symptoms
Know when to follow up if you don't feel better

phrases: I have a headache / stomachache / fever
How long have you felt this way?
target_language.grammar_pattern:
I have + symptom
My + body part + hurts
I feel + adjective

Examples:
- I have a headache
- My stomach hurts
- I feel sick
- Take this medicine two times a day

grammar_patterns.label: Doctor instructions
examples: Take this medicine two times a day
Take one pill in the morning

story.context: You are not feeling well. You go to the doctor at the clinic near your apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. How are you feeling today?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I feel sick. My head hurts.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Do you have a fever?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes. I feel hot and dizzy.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: How long have you felt this way?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Okay. Let me check. Open your mouth, please.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: You have the flu. I will give you medicine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. How do I take it?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Take one pill in the morning and one at night. You need to rest and drink a lot of water.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Come back in one week if you don't feel better.

drills.title: Drill 1: Describing symptoms
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct symptom
drills.your_turn: Now say what symptom you have (real or imagined) out loud and record it

drills.title: Drill 2: Saying what hurts
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct body part
drills.your_turn: Now say which body part hurts out loud and record it

drills.title: Drill 3: At the doctor
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank to complete the sentence
examples: I need to see a doctor.
drills.your_turn: Now describe how you feel to a doctor, out loud, and record it

listening.question: Listen: What is wrong with the patient?
listening.transcript: What is wrong today? My head hurts. I have a headache.
listening.explanation: The patient says 'My head hurts. I have a headache.'

listening.question: Listen: What does the doctor tell the patient to do?
listening.transcript: Please take this medicine and rest at home.
listening.explanation: The doctor says 'Take this medicine and rest.'

listening.question: Listen: How long has the person been sick?
listening.transcript: How long have you been sick? Three days.

speaking.title: Task 1: Describe your symptoms
speaking.instruction: Record yourself telling the doctor three symptoms: a headache, a fever, and a sore throat.
speaking.example: I have a headache. I have a fever. My throat hurts.

speaking.title: Task 2: Doctor visit conversation
speaking.instruction: Record a short conversation where you visit the doctor because your stomach hurts.
speaking.example:
Doctor: How are you feeling?
You: I feel sick. My stomach hurts.
Doctor: How long?
You: Two days.
Doctor: Take this medicine.
You: Thank you, doctor.

writing.title: Task 1: Write your symptoms
writing.instruction: Write 5 sentences describing different symptoms. Use 'I have...', 'My ... hurts', or 'I feel...'
writing.example:
1. I have a headache.
2. My back hurts.
3. I feel dizzy.
4. I have a fever.
5. My throat hurts.

writing.title: Task 2: Write a doctor visit
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (8-10 lines) where you visit the doctor because you feel sick.
writing.example:
Doctor: Hello. How are you feeling?
You: I feel sick.
Doctor: What is wrong?
You: My head hurts and I have a fever.
Doctor: How long?
You: Three days.
Doctor: Take this medicine two times a day.
You: Okay. Thank you.
Doctor: Come back in one week.
You: Thank you, doctor.

sections.title: Talking about symptoms with 'I have'
sections.question: What pattern do you see for telling the doctor what is wrong?
sections.explanation: We use 'I have + a + symptom' to describe what is wrong. Common symptoms: a headache, a fever, a stomachache, a cold, a cough.

sections.title: Saying what hurts
sections.question: How do we say which body part has pain?
sections.explanation: We use 'My + [body part] + hurts' to say where the pain is. This is very useful at the doctor.

sections.title: Describing how you feel
sections.question: How do we describe our general feeling?
sections.explanation: We use 'I feel + [adjective]' to describe our general condition. The doctor will often ask 'How do you feel?' or 'How are you feeling?'

sections.title: Understanding the Doctor's Instructions
examples: Take one pill in the morning.
sections.question: How does the doctor tell you what to do?
sections.explanation: Doctors often give instructions as commands, starting with the action verb: 'Take...', 'Rest...', 'Open...', 'Come back...'. No 'you' is needed at the start.

quiz.question: Your head hurts. What do you tell the doctor?
quiz.explanation: 'I have a headache' is the correct way to describe this symptom.

quiz.question: The doctor asks 'How are you feeling?' You are sick. You say:
quiz.explanation: 'I am feeling sick' or 'I feel sick' are both correct.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: My stomach ___.
quiz.explanation: We say 'My stomach hurts.' The body part is singular, so we use 'hurts'.

quiz.question: The doctor says 'Take one pill in the morning.' What does this mean?
options: Eat one pill when you wake up
Take the pill to the morning
Buy one pill in the morning
Give one pill in the morning
quiz.explanation: 'Take medicine' means to eat or swallow the medicine. 'In the morning' means when you wake up.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: I have a ___. (your body temperature is high)
quiz.explanation: A fever means your body temperature is high. You feel hot.

quiz.question: The doctor says 'You need to rest.' What should you do?
quiz.explanation: 'Rest' means to relax and sleep. The doctor wants you to stay home and get better.

quiz.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
quiz.explanation: 'I have a headache' is correct. We need 'a' before 'headache'.

quiz.question: You feel like the room is spinning. You say:
quiz.explanation: 'Dizzy' means feeling like the room is spinning. This is important to tell the doctor.

quiz.question: Write a 6-line conversation where you visit the doctor because you have a stomachache and a fever.
quiz.explanation: Your conversation should include: greeting, describing symptoms, doctor asking questions, and doctor giving advice.

quiz.question: Think about a time you were sick. Write 3 sentences describing how you felt using the phrases from this lesson.
quiz.explanation: Practice using real experiences. Example: I had a fever. My head hurt. I felt tired.

somali.description: Baro sida calaamadaha jirrada loo sharaxo, tilmaamaha dhakhtarkana loo fahmo
objectives: Sharax sida aad dareemayso (I have a headache / My stomach hurts)
Ka jawaab su'aalaha dhakhtarka ee calaamadaha jirrada
Ogow goorta aad dib u tagto dhakhtarka haddii aadan ka fiicnayn

sections.explanation: 'I have + a + calaamad' waxaan u isticmaalnaa si aan u sheegno waxa khaldan. Calaamadaha caadiga ah: a headache (madax-xanuun), a fever (qandho), a stomachache (calool-xanuun), a cold (hargab), a cough (qufac).
'My + [xubin jidhka] + hurts' waxaan u isticmaalnaa si aan u sheegno meesha xanuunku yahay. Tani aad bay faa'iido ugu leedahay dhakhtarka.
'I feel + [tilmaame]' waxaan u isticmaalnaa si aan u sharaxno xaaladdeena guud. Dhakhtarku wuxuu inta badan waydiiyaa 'How do you feel?' ama 'How are you feeling?'
Dhakhaatiirtu waxay badanaa bixiyaan amarro, iyagoo ka bilaabaya fal-weedhaha: 'Take...', 'Rest...', 'Open...', 'Come back...'. Uma baahnid 'you' bilowga.

target_phrases: Waxaan qabaa xanuun madaxeed / calool xanuun / qandho
Intee in le'eg ayay sidan kuu ahayd?
Waxaad u baahan tahay inaad nasato
dialogue: Haa, waan fahmay. Ma qandho baad qabtaa?
Haa. Waan kululaystay oo waan wareersanahay.
Intee in la eg ayaad sidan dareemaysaa?
Haa. Aan eego. Afkaaga kala fur, fadlan.
Waxaad qabtaa hargab. Waxaan ku siin doonaa dawo.
Subaxdii hal kiniin qaado, habeenkiina hal. Waxaad u baahan tahay inaad nasato oo aad cabto biyo badan.
Haddii aadan ka fiicnayn, hal usbuuc kadib soo noqo.

vocabulary.definition: marka jidhku uu ka kululaado caadiga ah sababtoo ah xanuun
dareenka ah in wax walba ay wareegayaan; aan degganayn
xanuun caadi ah oo leh qandho, qufac, iyo xanuun jidh
wax aad qaadato markaad xanuunsan tahay si aad u fiicnaato
kiniin yar oo wareegsan oo aad liqto
inaad nasato oo seexato si jidhku uu u fiicnaado
vocabulary.example: Waxaad u baahan tahay inaad nasato.

vocabulary.definition: when your body is hotter than normal because you are sick
feeling like everything is spinning; unsteady
a common sickness with fever, cough, and body aches
something you take to help you feel better when sick
a small, round piece of medicine you swallow
vocabulary.example: Take one pill in the morning.

vocabulary.definition: to relax and sleep so your body can get better
